d: Sprawling equatorial constellation home to prototype variable Mira, nearby solar analogue Tau Ceti, and M-dwarf benchmarks.

gaia-2452378776434477184.x: Single G-type dwarf (11.9 ly) hosting multiple candidate exoplanets and a prominent circumstellar debris disk.

hip-3419.x: Brightest star in Cetus, an orange giant star (96 ly) pulsating as an active X-ray emitter.

hip-14135.x: Cool red giant star marking the open jaws of the mythological sea monster.

gaia-2500734851146653312.x: Archetypal pulsating variable red giant and binary system (~300 ly), leaving a spectacular 13-light-year ultraviolet tail.

gaia-2461150714560126080.x: Spectroscopic binary orange giant star representing the belly of the whale.

hip-12706.x: Close binary star system situated in the head of Cetus.

gaia-2358524597030794112.x: Nearby active red dwarf (12.1 ly) hosting three compact terrestrial planets.

lhs-1140.x: Mid M-dwarf (48.8 ly) hosting temperate rocky exoplanet LHS 1140 b, a prime candidate for atmospheric characterization.

gaia-5140693571158739840.x: Binary red dwarf system (8.7 ly) paired with extreme flare star prototype UV Ceti.
